source.title: A selective role for dopamine in stimulus-reward learning.

confidence_rationale: Causal (dopamine-antagonist + fast-scan voltammetry) demonstration that incentive salience is a SEPARATE quantity from predictive value, and that it can be attributed to a discrete object-cue (the lever) versus the reward LOCATION (the food cup) -- the sign-tracker/goal-tracker split. This is the strongest available biological grounding for SD-057's central architectural move: separate goal-object (what) from goal-location (where) and bind a revaluable incentive quantity to the object identity. High source quality; mapping is conceptually strong but indirect (the paper studies individual-differences phenotypes, not an explicit per-object incentive layer).
failure_signatures: Whether incentive salience attaches to the object-cue (sign-tracking) or the goal-location (goal-tracking) is an individual-differences phenotype in this work, not a within-agent per-object layer -- so the paper supports the SEPARABILITY of object-incentive from location-prediction but does not by itself license a single architecture that maintains a per-object incentive token for every object.

Incentive-salience attribution here required dopamine-dependent learning over training; an REE per-object token that is seeded or revalued without a corresponding learning signal would diverge from this mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A reward-predicting cue can acquire two dissociable properties -- predictive value and incentive (motivational) value; dopamine is selectively required for the latter. In sign-trackers, incentive salience is attributed to the discrete lever-cue itself, which becomes an attractive 'motivational magnet' that is approached and engaged; in goal-trackers the same cue predicts reward but the animal instead approaches the food-delivery location.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-057 inserts a per-object incentive layer that binds a revaluable incentive token to a specific object IDENTITY (the SD-049 per-type tag) and separates goal-object (what) from goal-location (where), replacing the single z_goal attractor that conflated them. Flagel et al. give the biological warrant: incentive salience is a distinct, separately-controlled quantity that the brain attaches to a specific object-cue, and that attachment is dissociable from where the reward is delivered -- exactly the what/where separation SD-057 builds.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The object-vs-location dissociation in this paper is realised as a between-individual phenotype (sign- vs goal-trackers), not as an explicit within-agent per-object incentive store; it grounds the SEPARABILITY and object-binding of incentive salience but is silent on maintaining one revaluable token per object. Rat autoshaping with a single lever-cue and food reward -> REE multi-object foraging.
mapping.source_context: Rat Pavlovian autoshaping (lever-CS -> food-US); flupenthixol dopamine blockade; fast-scan cyclic voltammetry of accumbens dopamine; sign-tracker vs goal-tracker phenotypes.

confidence_components.notes: Causal + recording evidence in Nature, very high quality. Mapping discounted because the what/where separation is a phenotype contrast, not an explicit per-object layer; the architectural per-object token is REE's construct.
